title: The Kindly Portrait
premise: Beatrix Marchetti returns to the drowned village of Hollowmere to bury his twin sister Beatrice, only to find the coffin holds a stranger wearing his own face. The village's melted bell rings each dusk, and those who hear its song begin to forget themselves, verse by verse, until they walk into the old well that refills with something worse than water. Beatrix, a lifelong skeptic who survived by never belonging anywhere, must uncover why the village substituted him for his sister and learn the bell-song's suppressed final verse without singing it aloud. In the end he discovers the final verse is a name—his own—and that surviving means letting the village sing it instead, trading his identity for his life as the well takes the congregation that wronged his family a century ago.
about_author: Rafael Lockridge is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing defunct church records in rural England before turning to fiction. He writes horror about small communities that keep their bargains too well.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Coffin
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Arriving at Hollowmere, Beatrix views his twin's body and finds a man's corpse bearing his own features, aged twenty years. The undertaker insists it is Beatrice. Emotional beat: cold disbelief hardening into dread.

chapters.title: A Village That Remembers Him
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Strangers greet him by name, recall childhood debts he never incurred, and apologize for the funeral's haste. He corrects them; they smile pityingly. Emotional beat: gaslit isolation.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't Cast
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At dusk the church tower rings though records show the bell was melted in 1911; the tower has been open sky for decades. Only he seems to hear it. Emotional beat: first crack in his skepticism.

chapters.title: Verse One: The Water Rises
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. An old woman, Mrs. Aldery, hums the bell-song and forgets her son's name mid-sentence. Beatrix finds the song written in a hymnal with the last verse torn out. Emotional beat: protective urgency.

chapters.title: The Grave Digger's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Digging into parish records, he finds his family listed as buried here since 1890—generations before his birth. Emotional beat: uncanny vertigo at being pre-written.

chapters.title: The Well Refills Overnight
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The dry well behind the chapel brims with black water that reflects faces of people not standing there. A constable drowns in two feet of it. Emotional beat: the horror becomes physical.

chapters.title: What Beatrice Sent
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix via letters. Among his sister's effects, unsent letters describe her own visit months earlier and warn: 'They need a Marchetti who doesn't believe.' Emotional beat: grief sharpened into accusation.

chapters.title: The Congregation of the Drowned
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Night service in the roofless church; villagers sing the bell-song in unison while dry-eyed, mouths moving out of sync with sound. Emotional beat: revulsion and reluctant awe.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldery's Last Verse
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Dying, Aldery whispers that the torn verse names the one the bell wants, and begs him never to learn it whole. She dies mid-hum. Emotional beat: warning as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Already Buried
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He identifies the corpse as Elias Marchetti, missing since 1911—the last villager who heard the full song. Emotional beat: pattern recognition, and fear of fitting it.

chapters.title: Invisible Was a Skill
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix flashback. His childhood: learning to be unremarkable, to dodge attention, while Beatrice burned bright. Emotional beat: tenderness toward the twin whose brightness may have doomed her.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Innkeeper Coram admits the village traded 'a believer' to the well every generation for prosperity. They chose Beatrix because he'd never believe, and unbelief keeps the door shut from inside. Emotional beat: betrayal with logic he can't refute.

chapters.title: Verse Two: The Names Dissolve
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. More villagers lose their names after hearing the second verse; documents blank themselves. Beatrix's own signature begins fading from the guestbook. Emotional beat: identity eroding in real time.

chapters.title: The Archivist from Away
chapters.summary: POV new character, Dr. Imogen Vale, a folklorist arriving to study the bell legend. She hears nothing at dusk. Emotional beat: relief of an outside witness—briefly.

chapters.title: Two Skeptics, One Song
chapters.summary: POV alternating Beatrix/Vale. Vale confirms the 1911 melting but finds slag in the tower shaped like a bell's shadow. She begins humming without realizing. Emotional beat: alliance forming over shared denial.

chapters.title: The Well Shows Him Her
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The black water shows Beatrice alive beneath it, mouthing the final verse. He nearly leans in; Vale pulls him back. Emotional beat: longing weaponized.

chapters.title: Coram's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Drunk, Coram reveals the substitution: the village buried the stranger in Beatrice's place so the well would think its debt paid and take Beatrix later, gently. Emotional beat: rage curdling into understanding.

chapters.title: Verse Three: The Bell Learns Your Voice
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The bell begins ringing in Beatrix's own timbre. Villagers now mistake his voice on the phone for the bell's. Emotional beat: selfhood under siege.

chapters.title: Vale Hums the Third Verse
chapters.summary: POV Vale. She wakes singing, her research notes rewritten in another hand. She begs Beatrix to tie her hands at night. Emotional beat: terror of becoming the enemy's instrument.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He locates the hymnal's excised leaf sealed in the church foundation stone, guarded by villagers who no longer remember why they guard it. Emotional beat: the answer within reach and forbidden.

chapters.title: Midnight Excavation
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix/Vale. They break the stone; the page is legible except the crucial line, water-stained into illegibility. The bell tolls angrily all night. Emotional beat: hope punished.

chapters.title: The Well Takes Coram
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Coram, guilt-ridden, walks into the well singing, and the water level drops an inch per verse. The village wakes prosperous-looking and hollow. Emotional beat: the price made visible.

chapters.title: Beatrice's Voice From Below
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The well speaks in Beatrice's voice, reciting memories only she knew—then ones she couldn't have known. He stops trusting what he mourns. Emotional beat: grief corrupted.

chapters.title: The Village Votes
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Nameless villagers, led by whatever speaks through the bell, vote unanimously to give Beatrix to the well at the equinox. Kindly, apologetic, absolute. Emotional beat: horror of polite collective will.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He tries police, priest, county records; every institution's paper trail dissolves. He realizes justice here must be taken, not requested. Emotional beat: conversion from bystander to actor.

chapters.title: Vale's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: POV Vale. Fully claimed, Vale chooses to enter the well willingly, buying Beatrix three days, and leaves him her notebook: the final verse is a name, and names can be given, not just sung. Emotional beat: devastating gift.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Countdown structure. He searches Elias Marchetti's 1911 cottage and finds Elias's diary: he learned the verse, refused to sing it, and was kept 'kindly' underground for fifty years. Emotional beat: dread of precedent.

chapters.title: Elias Under the Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beneath the chapel floor, a bricked room; inside, remains clutching a copy of the verse with the name smudged by thumb-wear. Elias read it ten thousand times without speaking. Emotional beat: grim fellowship across a century.

chapters.title: The Verse Is a Vow
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Deciphering the diary, he understands: the final verse binds whoever sings it to become the bell's voice forever. The well doesn't want his death; it wants his consent. Emotional beat: the trap's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: They Come With Lanterns
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Equinox eve. The kindly congregation comes to escort him, singing verses one through three, leaving silence where four belongs. Emotional beat: being loved to death.

chapters.title: The Refusal at the Wellhead
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At the well he refuses to sing; the villagers sing his name for him, trying to complete the vow on his behalf. He covers his ears and the water rises out of the well itself. Emotional beat: defiance against a chorus.

chapters.title: Beatrice's Real Message
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Amid the flood-voices he finally hears the true Beatrice—not below, but in the letters' hidden acrostic: 'Don't save me. Save the name.' Emotional beat: grief resolving into instruction.

chapters.title: Giving the Name Away
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He realizes he can surrender the name 'Marchetti'—the village's claim—to the well without surrendering himself. He renounces it aloud, unbinding a century of debt. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: The Bell Sings Alone
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The bell, cheated of a singer, attempts the final verse itself and cracks along the 1911 fault-line. The song falters mid-word. Emotional beat: triumphant, terrible noise.

chapters.title: The Well Empties
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The black water drains, releasing a century of the nameless—Coram, Vale, Aldery, generations—who dissolve gratefully into morning fog. Beatrice's face is not among them; she was never there. Emotional beat: mourning without illusion.

chapters.title: Burial, Correct This Time
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He buries the stranger under Elias's name and Beatrice's coffin is sent home empty by his choice. The village wakes ordinary, poorer, free. Emotional beat: quiet restitution.

chapters.title: Who Is Left Standing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Asked his name by a passing surveyor, he hesitates—he gave Marchetti away—and answers with a new one, feeling it fit like borrowed clothes. Emotional beat: identity as chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Humming Habit
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Weeks later he catches himself humming the song and stops at verse three, always at verse three. Some knowledge stays in the body. Emotional beat: survival with scar tissue.

chapters.title: A Letter to No Address
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He writes to the dead sister he can finally stop searching for, telling her everything, and burns the letter at the dry well. Emotional beat: farewell as release.

chapters.title: The Last Verse, Unsung
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, coda. Leaving Hollowmere behind, he passes a distant church ringing a strange new bell, and does not listen. He has learned the song's last verse; he will die without singing it. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect peace.
